📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

New York has signed a new private listings bill, which means that properties will be required to be visible to the public as they hit the market unless the seller signs an informed opt-out consent.

Late last week, Gov. Kathy Hochul signed the Fair and Transparent Real Estate Listing Act. The language of the bill requires that real estate listings be marketed in "at least one other publication, platform or website that does not require payment" or for the consumer to work with the brokerage for access.

This follows a quick path through the state's Legislature, which approved the act in a noncontroversial vote in June. The Upcoming York State Association of Realtors® strongly supports the bill.

This becomes the latest crackdown on private listings, where a real estate agent markets a property to a limited list of buyers before making it public.

Recent findings suggest that fair housing advocates say private listings raise discrimination concerns. One study from Bright MLS found private listings take longer to sell and don't guarantee more money.

The listing must be accessible to the general public, "without limitation to a particular brokerage, franchise or select group of licenses." Also, there can't be restrictions on some or all of the details in the listing, according to the language of the bill.

Recent findings suggest that the bill doesn't require a seller or lister to hold open houses or public showings if it violates any state or federal laws related to health and safety. And sellers can opt out, by signing a form that explicitly warns them that the listing will have limited visibility and possible impact on the price they get.

New York can punish violators with a fine of up to $5,000 and suspension or revocation of  their real estate license.

Earlier this year, the state saw its inventory of homes for sale fall to a 30-year low.

It has been revealed that washington and Connecticut have passed similar laws this year. Each has generally similar language in their bills, which also allow for opt-outs. A study from Zillow found the sales price of private listings was 1.3% less than comparable sales on the multiple listing service, costing the seller an average of $4,230 per sale. (Realtor.com® recently struck an agreement with Zillow to show preview listings from brokers who participate in Zillow’s preview program, in an effort to boost market transparency.).

Recent findings suggest that compass Inc., the real estate brokerage giant which has defended its use of private listings, noted its recently unveiled See It First listings strategy complies with the law. It debuted that program in September, which gives early access to homes that will soon be listed on the public market. People don't need to work with a Compass agent to use it.

"Latest York’s new law preserves homeowners’ right to choose how they market their homes, including the ability to use a See It First strategy to test pricing and gauge demand," a Compass spokesperson remarked. "See It First early access homes comply with the new law and continue to give sellers flexibility in how and when they bring their homes to market.".

New York has long struggled with housing affordability. The Realtor.com State-by-State Housing Report Card gave the Empire State an F, the lowest rating possible. Hochul has emphasized affordability concerns and made a deregulation push to make home construction easier.

“My administration is focused on making New York more affordable and liveable for every New Yorker regardless of age or income, and housing is central to that goal,” Hochul noted last week.

Tristan Navera is a senior reporter on housing policy, covering trends and solutions in the housing market from Washington, DC. He was previously a senior reporter at Bloomberg Law, and before that covered real estate for the Washington Business Journal. Earlier in his career, he spent a decade reporting on business and real estate in Dayton and Columbus, OH. A Cincinnati native, he holds a journalism degree from Ohio University.

Long Before The U.S. Air Force Existed, The Army Used Planes Made By The Wright Brothers

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (501 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that with how ubiquitous commercial air travel is today it's easy to overlook how astonishingly rapid early aircraft development was.
  • In a recent development, the tactical advantage of holding the higher ground had been known for centuries, but aircraft opened up an entirely newly introduced dimension.
  • Army decided to revive this reconnaissance role when opening bidding for a two-seat observation aircraft in 1908.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that with how ubiquitous commercial air travel is today it's easy to overlook how astonishingly rapid early aircraft development was. There were only 24 years between the maiden flight of the Wright Flyer in 1903 and Charles Lindbergh made the first solo transatlantic flight in 1927. However, military thinkers were even quicker to realize the potential of powered flight on the battlefield. The U.S. Army purchased a Wright Military Flyer in 1909 for use as an observation aircraft. The first heavier-than-air military aircraft served as the spark that eventually led to creation of the U.S. Air Force, but it wasn't an unmitigated success.

In a recent development, the tactical advantage of holding the higher ground had been known for centuries, but aircraft opened up an entirely newly introduced dimension. Initially, it was hot air balloons taking to the wild blue yonder. During the Civil War, the Union Army fielded a balloon corps to perform reconnaissance and scout Confederate Army positions. The corps wouldn't last long with then-General Ulysses S. Grant dissolving the unit in August 1863.

The U.S. Army decided to revive this reconnaissance role when opening bidding for a two-seat observation aircraft in 1908. According to the U.S. Department of Defense, the Wright Military Flyer reached an altitude of 400 feet while averaging a speed of 42.5 miles per hour during its final ten-mile qualifying flight in July 1909. The service would purchase a single Wright Military Flyer for $30,000 next month. The sum would be $1.1 million today when adjusted for inflation.

Recent findings suggest that the demonstration campaign that convinced the U.S. Army Signal Corps to open its checkbooks wasn't flawless. Orville Wright would bring a Wright Model A plane to Fort Myer near Arlington National Cemetery in 1908. The younger Wright brother flew dignitaries on brief flights around the Fort's drilling grounds in front of over 2,000 people.

The spectacle was going perfectly until First Lieutenant Thomas Selfridge climbed abroad as a passenger. He had been the first U.S. Army officer to fly a plane just months earlier. According to Air & Space Magazine, Model A suffered a propeller failure while flying at 40 mph at an altitude of at least 100 feet. The twin-propeller wood and canvas biplane tumbled out of control and plummeted to the ground. Wright was seriously injured, but the crash killed Selfridge.

Sources indicate that in the crash's aftermath, a distraught Wright believed that he could've landed the plane safely if he had "a few feet more" of altitude. He returned to Fort Myer with an upgraded plane the next year and secured the sale to the Signal Corps. The Wright Military Flyer would never see combat, but it's easy to see how the early aircraft would've been vulnerable to machine gun fire from the ground with such a low maximum altitude. It wouldn't be the U.S. Army's last foray into experimental aircraft. The service would dabble in early drone warfare less than a decade later.

The True Cost of In-Port Emissions

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • How current shore power rules cost hundreds of millions every year in health and climate damages.
  • In a recent development, air pollution and climate emissions from ships at berth impose a heavy and unaddressed burden on European port communities and local economies.
  • Sources indicate that to quantify the cost of inaction, we evaluated at-berth emissions across the 100 largest EU ports using CE Delft’s Handbook on the External Costs of Transport.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

How current shore power rules cost hundreds of millions every year in health and climate damages.

In a recent development, air pollution and climate emissions from ships at berth impose a heavy and unaddressed burden on European port communities and local economies. While the Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR) took an important first step by mandating Onshore Power Supply (OPS) for large container and passenger vessels, several blind spots leave over half of all in-port emissions unregulated.

Sources indicate that to quantify the cost of inaction, we evaluated at-berth emissions across the 100 largest EU ports using CE Delft’s Handbook on the External Costs of Transport. Based on 2024 MRV data, in-port emissions cost €2.53 billion every year in health damages and climate abatement costs. Covering only the electricity demand from large unregulated ship types would already save €500 million annually, while tackling boilers would save another €714 million. Shipping companies effectively offload these costs onto public budgets, making fossil fuels appear artificially cheap. Once all impacts are counted, using electricity when at berth is half as expensive as burning fossil fuels.

Industry observers note that while AFIR successfully kickstarted early shore power roll-out, its narrow scope leaves significant volumes of emissions unaddressed. Beyond health and climate impacts, this partial coverage creates uncertainty and deprives port authorities, network operators , and investors from the predictability they need to develop and deploy the required infrastructure. Providing a clear time horizon for the provision of shore power to all ships is essential to share infrastructure costs, reduce electricity prices and permanently clean up air in ports.

By Eloi Nordé, Shipping Policy Officer, T&E.

Matters.AI raises $12M as it expands its data security business in North America

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (879 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Enterprise data security startup Matters.AI today confirmed that it has raised $12 million in latest funding as it expands its business in North America.
  • According to recent reports, matters.AI offers a platform called the AI Security Engineer for Data that is designed to protect sensitive data used by employees, artificial intelligence systems and AI agents across the enterprise.
  • In a recent development, AI agents, the company argues, now have the same access to enterprise data as the employees who run them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 17:22 EST / NOVEMBER 23 2026.

Enterprise data security startup Matters.AI today confirmed that it has raised $12 million in latest funding as it expands its business in North America.

According to recent reports, matters.AI offers a platform called the AI Security Engineer for Data that is designed to protect sensitive data used by employees, artificial intelligence systems and AI agents across the enterprise. Formerly known as OptiQ.AI, the manufacturer has teams in the San Francisco Bay Area and Bengaluru, India.

In a recent development, AI agents, the company argues, now have the same access to enterprise data as the employees who run them. Visibility into who or what is using that data is missing from most data security tools, according to Matters.AI, leaving security teams to connect alerts from separate tools by hand.

In a recent development, security teams using Matters.AI get one place to see where sensitive data resides, where it has traveled and who or what has accessed it. Data is tracked across cloud environments, on-premises systems, software-as-a-service applications, endpoints and browsers. The tech giant’s AI analyzes the context of that data and the intent behind each use.

Recent findings suggest that underneath that view, sensitive data across the data estate is discovered and classified, according to the company. Matters.AI also uses patented fingerprinting, built on large language models, to follow data as it moves between systems.

Insider risk and compliance risk are identified by correlating four signals, those being data sensitivity, misconfiguration, access and intent. Within policies set by the security team, the AI Security Engineer for Data is designed to gather the evidence on a flagged risk before remediating it on its own.

The platform is being pitched as a way to bring together work that enterprises typically buy as five separate products: data security posture management, data detection and response, database activity monitoring, data loss prevention and insider risk management.

Coming into its upcoming funding round, Matters.AI has been deployed at more than 50 organizations. Customers include major financial institutions, brokerage and asset management firms, large retailers and digital media and entertainment platforms, the organization claims.

Sources indicate that “Enterprises want to move fast with AI, but no one can trust an agent with data they cannot follow,” Harsh Sahu, co-founder and chief technology officer of Matters.AI, mentioned in the manufacturer’s announcement. According to Sahu, the platform works across petabytes of data and billions of access events a day.

Co-founder and Chief Executive Keshava Murthy argued that security teams do not need “another tool telling them something might be wrong,” adding that they instead need a system that can investigate a problem and take action.

Tanglin Venture Partners Pte. Ltd. led the pre-Series A round, with IIFL Fintech Fund, Piper Serica’s Bharat Tech Fund, Foster Ventures and Tetration Ventures also participating. Existing investors Kalaari Capital and Endiya Partners also invested in the round. The pair co-led a $4.75 million seed round announced in October 2025, when Matters.AI also disclosed an earlier $1.5 million pre-seed round led by Better Capital and Carya Venture Partners.

Sankalp Gupta, managing partner at Tanglin Venture Partners, stated that rather than “adding another layer of alerts, the team is rethinking how enterprise data security operates.”.

In a recent development, research and development in data lineage, autonomous investigation, endpoint and browser intelligence and the prevention of sensitive data misuse by AI agents will be the focus of the money raised. Including the latest funding, Matters.AI has raised $18.25 million to date.

5 Vehicles Recommended By Consumer Reports That Also Have Significant Black Friday Deals

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1576 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, let's ground your enthusiasm just a tad here.
  • Sources indicate that to square up that giant publisher's musts, the vehicles are weighed on factors like how they perform on the site's road tests.
  • Consumer Reports also gives higher ratings for standard active safety tech.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, let's ground your enthusiasm just a tad here. Consumer Reports (CR) just came out with a list of a dozen 2026 models that at the moment offer steep Black Friday discounts. The organization is highlighting these deals because every whip on its list also received a strong overall score in Consumer Reports' testing. We have our own take on which vehicles we'd chase hardest, however, so we'll edit CR's edit.

Sources indicate that to square up that giant publisher's musts, the vehicles are weighed on factors like how they perform on the site's road tests. And to earn a higher rating, cars that CR recommends need to have performed well in the owner surveys it conducts on hundreds of thousands of cars — the organization wants its readers to consider whether they'd buy the same car again if they had the chance. It also prefers vehicles that get better marks from the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS).

Consumer Reports also gives higher ratings for standard active safety tech. This includes automatic emergency braking, blind-spot warning systems, and rear cross-traffic warning systems. And the publication gives props to vehicles that come with camera systems that monitor the driver for attentiveness. The outlet layers on extra credit if the IIHS claims a car does well in its front crash protection tests for pedestrians. Consumer Reports' recommended rating also comes down to predicted reliability, again based on reader surveys.

Still, we've got our own take here, and we do a deeper dive on the discount fine print as well as sift their dozen choices down to an odd five cars — just because a car's cheaper doesn't mean you want it in the driveway for the next decade.

The American-made Honda Ridgeline qualifies for some hefty incentives. Consumer Reports found discounts equaling up to $4,953. That's probably due to varied incentives offered by different dealers. For example, you can find $2,250 off via a national incentive directly from Honda, while Carsdirect highlights up to $2,750 off and 1.99% financing for 36 months. While a three-year loan means paying more per month than a longer term, 1.99% is far lower than the latest national average rate of 7.3% — meaning you'd be spending far less to pay off your Honda.

Poke around at area dealers, too. We found a deal offering at least $3,045 off of the Ridgeline, which actually exceeds the deal tallied by Consumer Reports, courtesy of Friendly Honda in New York's Hudson Valley. There's another way to save on the Ridgeline after you make the purchase. See, the truck is listed on Consumer Reports' top USA-made cars list, which could unlock some major loan deductions. The way that works is that if you purchase a qualifying American-made vehicle, the IRS gives you a tax credit of up to $10,000 on the interest paid on the loan for that new truck. On the Ridgeline, we arrived at a $5,633 in deductions.

It has been revealed that even without the tax credit, getting several thousand bucks off the Ridgeline makes it extra compelling. We praised its handling in our review of the off-road-focused Honda Ridgeline Trailsport, and we dig its ride quality. Ford's Maverick didn't make Consumer Reports' best cars made in America list, but this Honda wins for that, and we like it for out-towing the Ford, too.

According to recent reports, earlier this year, we put the Hyundai Elantra on our list of the cheapest new cars on the market for 2026. You, dear reader, also voted the Elantra onto your list of the best value cars, too. Consumer Reports found potential deals of up to $2,958 off the Elantra SEL's $23,950 MSRP before destination costs. Our own research highlights $2,000 back from Hyundai nationally, while some individual dealers such as Danbury Hyundai in Connecticut have an additional $500 available for recent college graduates and another $500 for first responders.

According to recent reports, as for why you like it — you actually prefer the Elantra Hybrid. The bummer there is that there's only a $500 discount off the $26,650 base price of that more fuel-efficient version of the Elantra. We get the thinking: We praised the Hybrid for being quieter and riding better than the non-hybrid, but don't forget that the base SE runs $24,120 with destination, before the $2,000 discount.

It has been revealed that previously, we praised the standard feature set, including an 8.0-inch touchscreen display, the fact that it gets standard wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, and of course, Consumer Reports likes that it also comes baked with a blind-spot warning system, rear cross-traffic warning, and automatic emergency braking with pedestrian detection, as well as lane keeping. Oh, and if you're lanky, the Elantra easily fits taller drivers thanks to 40.6 inches of headroom and 42.3 inches of legroom.

In a recent development, we don't know how Hyundai will price the next-generation Elantra – which feels too nice to be treated like an economy car. That may mean it won't be as affordable come this time next year, so you should probably buy one now, before prices climb.

Consumer Reports found savings of $4,852 off the 2026 Santa Fe. We found that Hyundai is offering a $3,000 national program plus 0% interest loans for up to 60 months, which is a very good way to save a lot of money on the carrying costs of a newly introduced car. Look around for other dealer incentives, too. We also found another $2,004 off offered by Ontario Hyundai in the Los Angeles area, knocking nearly $5,000 off the Santa Fe SEL's $40,075 sticker.

It has been revealed that we dig the Santa Fe for lots of reasons. Back in 2024, we called it boxy and beautiful from every angle and praised Hyundai for moving from its frumpy curves to a more chiseled bod. Then there's the combination of utility — since it seats up to seven humans — and the fact that the interior is well designed and comfortable. We crowned it the crossover to end all crossovers, too, in part because we really love the dual-clutch transmission and the Santa Fe's superb ride.

If you're instead chasing fuel economy, Hyundai's $3,000 off the 2026 Santa Fe Hybrid is a better price cut than the carmaker's offering for the Elantra Hybrid. At $40,380, the 2026 Santa Fe Hybrid still pulls a big premium over the non-hybrid, but you can qualify for the same 0% interest loan for 60 months.

Audi's A3 and S3 are cars we can't help but drool over. That's partly because they're sports sedans, which is a dying breed. Audi is at the moment offering up to $3,500 off the sticker price of the A4 and $2,500 off the S3. That nudges the $41,495 A3's sticker (after destination) just beneath $40,000. However, the $53,395 S3 only gets a minor haircut.

It has been revealed that we noted back in 2025, when the Audi A3 and S3 underwent their most recent refresh, that that the cars are really petite — about three inches shorter than the Honda Civic. And yet we claimed that the Audi S3 is all the car you'll ever need. Our review of the S3 dovetails with why Consumer Reports likes the lower-tier A3, saying it outperforms peers like the BMW 2 Series Gran Coupe and Mercedes-Benz CLA. A base, 201-horsepower inline-four provides reasonable power in the A3, and while Consumer Reports doesn't love the car's dual-clutch transmission, we found this seven-speed gearbox delightful.

It has been revealed that note that this is a driver's car, first. We praised the driver's seat for its support, and so did Consumer Reports — but they handed a demerit to the squished nature of the rear perches. Did we mention it's smaller than a Honda Civic?

You can get up to $4,500 off the Rogue Platinum and $3,500 off lower-tier Rogues, but hunt a bit. We found $3,000 off a Rogue SV with a national incentive, plus another $950 from Poughkeepsie Nissan in Fresh York. That knocked the total sticker down to $31,235. Then again, at a different dealer in Los Angeles, prices are sliding $3,000 across the table alongside $3,500 from Nissan, which drops the sticker of a Rogue SV from $32,500 down to $26,122. Even if you don't live in L.A., maybe it's worth flying out to buy that Nissan.

As for the Rogue's attributes, they're good, if not revolutionary. The new-for-2027 Rogue Hybrid, however, is a total game-changer thanks to an entirely reinvented hybrid system, where we said its silence speaks volumes, because it operates way more like a pure EV. That said, the 1.5-liter turbocharged inline-three beneath the hood of the 2026 Rogue is still plenty punchy, with 201 hp. Key to that sensation is low-end torque of 225 pound-feet hitting at 2,800 rpm and sticking around through 4,000 rpm.

It has been revealed that we noted that the Nissan's inline-3 delivers power more like what you'd expect from a larger V6, but the bonus is you're not pushing all those extra pistons. That means the FWD Rogue gets a combined 32 mpg while the AWD model gets 31 mpg. That's not the 38 mpg Nissan expects from its latest Rogue Hybrid, but if you can nab a 2026 Rogue for $26,000 versus the $37,065 tab on that latest-and-greatest Nissan, we're guessing you'll be just fine with that trade-off.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • There are various opinions on the Chinese auto market, as shown recently in discussions under this article, but no matter what your opinion is on the Chinese economy and auto market, you have to recognize that Chinese automakers — driven by their electric leaders — are gaining more market share quickly in markets around the world, while legacy automakers from the US, Europe, and Japan are losing market share.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are various opinions on the Chinese auto market, as shown recently in discussions under this article, but no matter what your opinion is on the Chinese economy and auto market, you have to recognize that Chinese automakers — driven by their electric leaders — are gaining more market share quickly in markets around the world, while legacy automakers from the US, Europe, and Japan are losing market share.

In particular, I just saw a headline highlighting that Chinese automakers have overtaken Japanese automakers in 6 more countries this year. That adds to the 20 markets where Chinese automakers had already surpassed Japanese automakers in market share. One thousand bonus points to anyone who can guess the six upcoming markets before scrolling past the image below.

Sources indicate that the fresh markets where Chinese automakers are now outselling Japanese ones are: Brazil, Ghana, Italy, South Korea, Tunisia, and the United Kingdom. Again, these are spread across the globe about as much as possible. Chinese auto companies, especially due to their insanely competitive electric vehicles, are overtaking the old guard in one corner of the world after another.

This news comes to us from data from Mobility Global, via the South China Morning Post. “Chinese carmakers stand out for their competitive pricing, EV portfolios and market-specific advantages such as localisation, remarked Tatiana Hristov, the company’s director of global vehicle sales forecasts,” SCMP reports.

Of course, EV demand has also risen due to the ongoing oil wars going on in the world, most notably now the US war on Iran. “Chinese brands benefit in particular because they are normally cheaper, so they are more attractive to consumers who are increasingly price sensitive under the oil shock,” noted Xu Tianchen, an economist at the Economist Intelligence Unit. “Chinese brands benefit in particular because they are normally cheaper, so they are more attractive to consumers who are increasingly price sensitive under the oil shock.” Good point.

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Like missions and side quests, stealing cars has always been an integral part of the "Grand Theft Auto" franchise.
  • While you can still do things the old-fashioned way, like pulling the driver out and taking control of the vehicle, or smashing a window, hotwiring the car, and driving away, those methods won't necessarily work on every car across the fictional state of Leonida.
  • How can you tell if a car is keyless or has a tracker installed?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Like missions and side quests, stealing cars has always been an integral part of the "Grand Theft Auto" franchise. For "GTA 6," not only have the developers leaned into advanced physics for more realistic car crashes, but car theft itself has evolved into multiple tiers.

While you can still do things the old-fashioned way, like pulling the driver out and taking control of the vehicle, or smashing a window, hotwiring the car, and driving away, those methods won't necessarily work on every car across the fictional state of Leonida. For example, keyless cars can't be hotwired. Even if someone left the doors of their expensive sports car open, you can't simply waltz in and drive away without a key cloner, which you'll only get access to later in the game. Standard and advanced vehicle trackers are also something to keep in mind. (Minor progression spoilers ahead.).

How can you tell if a car is keyless or has a tracker installed? Enter the WAiNK app. Your friend Cal installs it on your phone during a story mission in Chapter 1. The app lets you scan a car to see its make and model and whether it's locked, alarmed, keyless, or fitted with a tracker. Additionally, the app tells you the car's condition, how much it's worth, and what it costs to register should you wish to own it. Keep in mind that although registering stolen cars is how you take ownership of them in "GTA 6," that feature won't be unlocked until Chapter 2, when you meet Moses, who gifts you a slim jim.

Industry observers note that to steal cars without breaking the window or setting off the alarm, you'll need to use a slim jim. It works through a lock-picking minigame when you interact with a locked, unoccupied vehicle. While the method is unlikely to attract unwanted attention, it still won't let you start cars with keyless ignition. For that, you'll need to wait until you're about halfway through Chapter 3, at which point you'll get a key cloner. (It's a phone app you download during a story mission.).

According to recent reports, the process itself is similar to using the slim jim, and once it's done, the door unlocks, and you drive away — no need to hotwire the car. As mentioned earlier, you can use the WAiNK app before you try to steal a car to see which sort of tracker it has, among other details. Standard trackers are not that massive of a deal — the catch is that you can't take the car to a mod shop for any kind of modifications unless you've registered it as your own.

According to recent reports, cars with advanced trackers, on the other hand, alert the police and pinpoint your location — remember, "GTA 6" has flock-like cameras to track your movements. You'll have to drive really fast to stop the tracker from sending the location signal to the cops. If you slow down, the tracker starts beeping, and you only have a few seconds to speed up before it gives away your location. And, unlike in older "GTA" games, cars in "GTA 6" don't have infinite gas, so keep that in mind as well.

The 54-year-old actress shared a look at her holiday decorations on Instagram, revealing that even her greenhouse got a festive touch with a wreath of its own.

It has been revealed that thanksgiving preparations were underway in the kitchen, where Garner gave the turkey a trial run ahead of the substantial day. Her dogs and cat were dressed for the occasion, too, in turkey costumes.

“We’re ready over here,” Garner wrote in the caption.

Recent findings suggest that garner has been known to love the holiday season, having previously opened up about her favorite memories during a Nov. 4 episode of the "Happy Hour With Ina Garten" podcast.

“My favorite Thanksgivings were when my kids were really little, I think it was right at the end of 'Alias,' and it was at a big house,” said Garner, who shares Violet, 20, Seraphina, 17, and Samuel, 14, with her ex-husband Ben Affleck.

In a recent development, “My kids were little, and Ben and I were there, and we all cooked. Bradley made the stuffing and Victor made ... I think Victor’s sister came. It was just our little 'Alias' family cooking together. It was so special," she added, referring to her co-stars Victor Garber, Ron Rifkin, and Bradley Cooper.

Despite separating in 2015 and divorcing in 2018, Garner and Affleck have continued to celebrate the holidays together.

Last year, a source told People that the couple spent the holidays together in Los Angeles.

Recent findings suggest that “Jen makes it very special. She’s such a great chef. She loves having her whole family together, too. Ben’s always welcome at her house,” the source told the outlet.

Garner is known for showing off touching memories at her dwelling.

Last year, Garner and her mom were brought to tears when they were surprised with a near-perfect re-creation of the kitchen that sat inside the actress' childhood home in West Virginia.

Garner and her mom, Patricia Ann, couldn't help but get emotional when they were brought to the space, which had been designed by appliance tech giant KitchenAid to perfectly mirror the kitchen of their Charleston, WV, home.

The mother-daughter duo initially thought they were being brought in to take part in a holiday photo shoot, but after stepping inside the kitchen set, which looked identical to the one in their Greystone Place abode, they were left gobsmacked.

Both Garner and her mom began welling up at seeing their vintage wooden table and green refrigerator, with both women rapidly recalling the happy memories they had made in the original space.

In a recent development, “This is where we would hang out, all our crafts happened right here with somebody looking through from that side," Garner mentioned, while looking through the cupboards. "This is the cabinet where you hid the chocolate chips.".

The kitchen boasted a large wooden table, matching wooden cabinets, yellow oven, granite countertops, drawings, and a yellow KitchenAid mixer.

The "13 Going on 30" star then pointed at a nostalgic photo of her mom that was placed on the counter. It reminded her of the days that Patricia would get her perm done while "sitting at the table.".

Sources indicate that “It’s a privilege to get to see where we used to be. I want that to be the den, and then I want to hear dad come home from work. That’s what I feel," Patricia said.

The 87-year-old noted that the patterned wallpaper in the replica kitchen first caught her eye.

Garner noted that the experience gave her a "really deep feeling of homesickness and gratitude.".

Patricia previously joined her daughter on Garner's latest installment of her "Pretend Cooking Show.".

Tesla Wants You To Watch Its 'Reality View' Instead Of Paying Attention To Reality

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (386 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There's little Tesla loves more than a dumb little party trick, and it often includes upcoming gimmick functionality within major updates to its software.
  • In a recent development, the Tesla faithful call the software revision V15, after the FSD version included, but the full package is known as Update 2026.38.6.11 — not exactly a name that rolls off the tongue.
  • According to recent reports, FSD 15 can see chain link fence and power lines!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's little Tesla loves more than a dumb little party trick, and it often includes upcoming gimmick functionality within major updates to its software. The recent release of V15, software for Tesla's latest in-car computers, adds another trick: A new camera angle that reveals the car from a third-person view, like in a video game. Tesla calls it Reality View, and out of everything a Tesla can do, it sure is one of the things.

In a recent development, the Tesla faithful call the software revision V15, after the FSD version included, but the full package is known as Update 2026.38.6.11 — not exactly a name that rolls off the tongue. The update did include functional changes to FSD, mostly relating to the computer vision wall Tesla keeps beating its head against, but it seems the engineers had a thought while working on all those cameras: Why not use them to simulate a third-person view, like a video game?

According to recent reports, FSD 15 can see chain link fence and power lines! 🤯🙌🏽 @Tesla @TeslaSI @elonmusk pic.twitter.com/m3fn7c4obA.

Initially, after looking at both Tesla's demo footage and footage from real owners, I figured the car was using SpaceXAI's models to generate a third-person view based on the input from the cameras — a method that would explain some of the odd glitches and scale issues present in some of the clips as AI hallucinations. According to Elon Musk's tweets, that's exactly what's going on — rather than an actual display of what the car's cameras and FSD software see, Tesla owners are now treated to an AI-generated picture of what's going on around them.

Recent findings suggest that the ability to mesh multiple cameras into a single point of view like this is neat, and the underlying tech is impressive, though it's unclear how much compute is needed to generate these images, and what kind of load that puts on the car. What these images aren't, though, are replacements for the actual data visualization that FSD used to supply. Even Tesla owners are admitting confusion between objects the car does and doesn't see with the newly introduced display. Most Tesla party tricks are some ratio of neat to useless, but this one genuinely appears to make the user experience of FSD worse.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that server maker Hewlett-Packard Enterprise Co.
  • Recent findings suggest that the company reported fourth-quarter earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of $1.43 per share, easily beating Wall Street’s target of $1.26 per share.
  • HPE also recorded a net profit of $1.82 billion, up from just $175 million in the year-ago period.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 18:24 EST / NOVEMBER 23 2026.

Sources indicate that server maker Hewlett-Packard Enterprise Co. posted its fastest quarterly revenue growth on record and raised its full-year forecast, but it wasn’t enough to keep up the momentum of a broader Nvidia Corp.-fueled rally, and its stock was headed lower after-hours.

Recent findings suggest that the company reported fourth-quarter earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of $1.43 per share, easily beating Wall Street’s target of $1.26 per share. Revenue for the period rose 50% from the same period one year earlier, to $14.55 billion, surpassing the Street’s $14.47 billion estimate.

HPE also recorded a net profit of $1.82 billion, up from just $175 million in the year-ago period.

In a recent development, the stunning revenue growth was a reflection of the enormous demand for artificial intelligence servers and networking equipment, noted President and Chief Executive Antonio Neri (pictured). “Our record performance reflects the portfolio we have built to drive durable, profitable growth for our shareholders,” he said in a statement.

It has been revealed that HPE stated it’s raising its revenue expectations for fiscal 2027, which ends next October, saying it’s now targeting growth of between 27% to 35%, or sales of between $59.4 billion and $63.1 billion. Previously, the company had been looking for growth of just 13% to 17%.

Neri told analysts on a conference call that the updated guidance reflects the growing demand the manufacturer is seeing for AI servers that extends well into next year. He said the company has a strong position as the AI industry shifts from a focus on training models to supporting inference workloads and AI agents.

“We have a perfect portfolio to capture that inflection point across networking, cloud and AI,” Neri stated, citing “the durability of the demand and the durability of our execution now with a completely different setup in our portfolio.” According to Neri, the improved outlook also reflects the company’s view that the supply of key components such as memory, flash and networking equipment will remain constrained through to the end of calendar 2028.

According to recent reports, despite the impressive forecast, HPE couldn’t sustain the momentum of an Nvidia-inspired rally that helped its stock jump more than 17% in regular trading before the earnings report. AI stocks in general received a huge boost earlier today on the news that the chipmaker has reinstated its founder and CEO Jensen Huang. But HPE fell more than 6% after-hours.

Sources indicate that holger Mueller of Constellation Research remarked most investors were probably happy enough with HPE’s results. “It’s building on its momentum with the second generation of its HPE Machine that was co-engineered with Nvidia,” the analyst said. “The tech giant is one of only two viable options for enterprises to run Nvidia workloads on-premises, and that is the reason for its record growth numbers. Going forward, investors will want to see the AI share of revenue increase steadily.”.

Recent findings suggest that for the current quarter, HPE is looking for revenue of between $14 billion and $14.6 billion, which would represent growth of 54% at the middle of that forecast. That suggests its revenue growth is going to accelerate and set a newly introduced manufacturer record. That forecast is strong too, with Wall Street analysts looking for first-quarter sales of just $13 billion.

HPE’s biggest rival in the AI server business, Dell Technologies Inc., is expected to announce its own earnings results tomorrow afternoon, along with HP, Nutanix and Workday.

Aetna is rolling out a upcoming program that aims to provide key end-to-end care for pregnant women, new mothers and infants.

Industry observers note that the offering, called Aetna For You and Baby, will be available to all expectant mothers enrolled in an Aetna plan. Through the program, moms will be connected to a prenatal visit in their first trimester and a postpartum visit within 12 weeks of the baby's birth.

Women in the program will also be screened for depression both during and after pregnancy to identify any risks.

In addition to supporting the mother both during pregnancy and postpartum, the program aims to give babies a healthy start by providing at least six well visits through their first 15 months, which offer critical tests and screenings, checkups and vaccinations.

The news of the launch was provided first to Fierce Healthcare.

Katerina Guerraz, Aetna's chief operating officer, told Fierce that maternal care often focuses mostly, if not completely, on labor and delivery, though prenatal and postpartum visits play a critical role in driving positive health outcomes.

In its announcement, Aetna notes that data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention show that about 90% of pregnancy-related deaths could have been prevented, with a lack of access to prenatal care and more complete support making for a key barrier.

"This is a national access glitch, a quality issue, and it's an affordability problem," she remarked.

In addition, it's not uncommon for programs that aim to drive better maternal outcomes to lack services for the babies, who in the first year of life undergo a wide array of critical developmental milestones, Guerraz noted.

Aetna, as the third-largest insurer in the U.S., sees about 200,000 deliveries a year among its members. That means the success of this program could have a significant impact in a short amount of time, supporting at least 1 million babies over the next five years, she said.

Sources indicate that aetna for You and Baby also builds on a broader push within the company to build a more personalized and simple experience for members. For instance, the company established a program that embeds Aetna nurses in the hospital to support discharge planning and transitions for members, and Guerraz noted that holds potential in the maternal care space.

For example, if a baby needs to stay in the neonatal intensive care unit after birth, having an Aetna nurse in the NICU providing additional support to the clinical team and the member would pay dividends, she stated.

Aetna is also plugged into Health 100, a sister subsidiary of its parent company, CVS Health, that offers an AI-powered tool to help patients identify healthcare costs and navigate their benefits, even if they're not members of Aetna or Caremark or CVS Pharmacy customers.

Guerraz said the program is designed to offer something that patients can carry with them if their coverage changes.

She added that the team intends to continue iterating on the program and identifying other barriers to care for moms and their babies.

"This is something that we know is going to have a massive impact," she stated.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes
Healthcare purchasers must weigh hospital quality alongside their prices, Leapfrog notes" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

Patient safety watchdog The Leapfrog Group released its latest collection of hospital safety grades hand-in-hand with calls for policymakers and stakeholders to consider, or directly tie patient safety reporting to price transparency.

The twice-yearly release brought top marks for 900 out of a total 2,366 graded hospitals, and the lowest “F” score for just three. There were 774 hospitals that earned a “B” grade, 655 a “C” grade, and 35 a “D” grade.

Recent findings suggest that no grades were assigned to another 447 hospitals, a decision the group made after a judge’s ruling in a lawsuit involving the scores it would assign to facilities that did not voluntarily submit their quality data to Leapfrog’s survey (Leapfrog appealed that decision in September). Leapfrog’s decision not to score these has generally shifted its letter grade distribution upward, and the organization has said it is reviewing a potential methodology change for upcoming gradings to incorporate non-submitting hospitals.

Still, “a record number of hospitals are choosing to publicly report their safety and quality performance, and we applaud them for holding themselves accountable to their patients,” Leapfrog President and CEO Leah Binder mentioned in a statement.

At the state level, Connecticut maintained its claim on the largest portion of hospitals earning an “A” grade (64.3% of its total), followed by Utah, Upcoming Jersey and South Carolina. Leapfrog also called out Rhode Island and Maine for jumping up the rankings—from eighteenth to seventh for the former, and from seventeenth to eighth for the latter. No hospitals were given an “A” grade in five states: Iowa, North Dakota, South Dakota, Vermont and Wyoming.

In a recent development, A hospital’s assigned grade is calculated by reviewing recent data on up to 22 patient safety measures, including a 10-part Medicare composite of reported patient safety and adverse events. Safety scores for specific hospitals can be searched on the group’s website.

Leapfrog and Binder, in a news release outlining its latest scores, made the case that its grades and similar independent measures warrant a seat at the table in a transparency conversation primarily focused on hospital costs.

It has been revealed that “Progress on price transparency is notable, but there’s no good price for bad care,” Binder said. “We are calling on the Trump Administration and Congress to ensure price transparency is integrated with patient safety and quality transparency.”.

The group backed its calls by pointing to a recent analysis (PDF) conducted by the Purchaser Business Group on Health (PBGH) that reviewed employer claims, federal price transparency data, and quality and safety measures including Leapfrog’s. It “found little to no correlation between negotiated prices and standardized quality measures,” as hospitals that received high safety grades often charged cheaper prices than those in the same market with lower grades.

Leapfrog and Elizabeth Mitchell, president and CEO of PBGH, stated the analysis—presently being expanded for practical usage by healthcare purchasers—is an example of how a more wholistic view of prices and care delivery should be considered when weighing a hospital.

“Employers have an appropriate duty to pay a fair price for high-quality care, and they can’t meet it by looking at price alone,” Mitchell remarked in the release from Leapfrog. “When we put the data together, some of the most expensive hospitals were not the safest. Our members want to buy high-quality, safe care that is fairly priced. That shouldn’t be too much to ask.”.

Florida court tosses Tampa General Hospital's suit against Eli Lilly over 340B discounts" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

A Florida federal court has tossed Tampa General Hospital's lawsuit against Eli Lilly over the 340B drug discount program.

Sources indicate that florida's Middle District court dismissed the case on a motion from the drugmaker on Wednesday. If Tampa General Hospital wants to file an amended complaint, it must do so within 30 days.

The hospital initially sued the pharmaceutical firm over a policy it implemented that requires providers to submit claims-level data on pharmacy and medical dispensing if they participate in 340B. Lilly stated it would pull back discounts for providers that did not comply with the requirement and has done so for several organizations, drawing ire from the industry.

Tampa General said the decision is "unconscionable and immoral" in the initial complaint, filed in July.

According to recent reports, however, the district court argued that Supreme Court precedent holds that organizations like hospitals do not have the private right to sue if they have been charged beyond the threshold, based on a 2011 decision. SCOTUS said that the right to sue was not outlined by Congress, so it is not an avenue available to these organizations.

"The Court made clear that there is simply no private remedy to superintend the pricing and provision of these discounted drugs," per the order.

"To permit this suit would be to encourage piecemeal litigation and defeat the [Supreme] Court’s insistence on maintaining the Congressional plan 'harmoniously and on a uniform, nationwide basis,'" according to the document.

Eli Lilly cheered the decision in a statement.

"Today’s decision is an notable step toward a more transparent 340B program," a Lilly spokesperson said. "Lilly’s claims data requirement asks hospitals for basic information—information they already give insurers every day—to prevent unlawful duplicate discounts.".

Sources indicate that "Decades of HRSA guidance and two federal appeals courts confirm that Lilly can lawfully require this information," the drugmaker mentioned. "More than 3,200 hospitals and clinics already share it with Lilly, and we hope Tampa General Hospital will join them.".

Tampa General Hospital has sued Eli Lilly and Firm over the drugmaker’s “unconscionable and immoral” rescindment of discounted pricing under the 340B program.

It has been revealed that the complaint, filed last week for the U.S. District Court in the Middle District of Florida, is early legal fallout from a policy Lilly implemented earlier this year that requires providers participating in the federal subsidy program to submit claims-level data for all pharmacy and medical dispensations. The tech giant threatened to pull the discounts for those that didn’t comply and made good on its threat for a subset of hospitals last month, sparking outrage among provider groups.

According to recent reports, tampa General, a nearly 1,000-bed disproportionate share hospital, confirmed in the legal complaint that it was among those cut off. It is now spending 25% to 50% more on average for Lilly products, “many of which it must purchase because of Lilly’s status as the market’s only supplier of a given drug product.”.

It has been revealed that tampa General’s lawsuit frequently describes Lilly in such terms, framing the drugmaker as holding significant monopoly power and wielding it in violation of the Florida Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act. It also often draws contrast to the 340B program’s intent to support the margins of safety-net hospitals providing care to vulnerable patients, against Lilly’s current status as the largest pharmaceutical organization in the world by market cap.

A spokesperson for Lilly, in a statement given to Fierce Healthcare, described the lawsuit as “just another part of the broader hospital campaign to fight transparency and hide the fraud, waste and abuse that plague the 340B program.”.

In a recent development, tampa General asked the court to order an immediate end to Lilly’s policy and to award damages for the higher prices to which the hospital was subjected. It contends Lilly’s alleged failure to comply with 340B pricing requirements and decision to continue marketing its products as 340B-discounted are unfair trade practices under the Florida statute.

“The most valuable pharmaceutical manufacturer in the world is engaged in a campaign to transfer dollars earmarked for charitable purposes into its own pocket,” the complaint reads. “The direct and inevitable result of Lilly’s actions is reduced healthcare for poor people. Its actions shock the conscience and are self-evidently unconscionable.”.

Tampa General, similar to the hospital associations that have protested Lilly’s policy, contends that the claims data it requires imposes substantial administrative burden on 340B providers. Even “hospitals who have caved to Lilly’s latest demands” have effectively had the prices for their covered outpatient drugs increased due to those administrative costs, it wrote in the complaint.

Lilly and other drugmakers who have signaled similar plans have said they need claims data to spot instances in which a drug purchase is improperly granted multiple discounts under overlapping programs. The company has also disputed that the burden of its policy is as substantial as hospitals say.

Industry observers note that “The claims data Lilly requires hospitals to share is information they already collect and send to insurers regularly,” the Lilly spokesperson mentioned of the lawsuit’s claims. “Refusing to share that same data with Lilly highlights that hospitals are more concerned with hiding rampant abuse in the program than improving its integrity. Lilly will keep working to ensure this program serves vulnerable patients instead of hospitals and their for-profit partners.”.

Recent findings suggest that the 340B program has proven to be a magnet for industry and policy conflict, particularly in recent years as its scale has ballooned. The divide is most evident in the ongoing clash over a pilot rebate program that the Trump administration attempted to launch at the top of the year but was forced to restart after the hospital industry’s legal pushback.

340B providers also received a shock this past week when the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services floated a significant reduction in its 340B reimbursement to 33.4% below average sales price in its annual proposed rule on hospital outpatient payments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Meghan Markle and Prince Harry plan to host Meghan’s mother for the holidays at their newly introduced U.K. home, where Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet will celebrate their first Christmas in Britain.

A trip to California had been a possibility, but the Duke and Duchess of Sussex intend to spend both Thanksgiving and Christmas in Britain after six years on the West Coast.

Doria Ragland is expected to join them, and Harry suspects his mother-in-law will have a hand in the holiday menu.

Industry observers note that “My wife is very good in the kitchen and so is my mother-in-law, so I’ll leave that to them,” Harry, 42, said during a Nov. 20 appearance on the British morning show "This Morning.".

He did have one dish on his mind.

“Maybe gumbo, yeah, maybe turkey, maybe gumbo,” he said.

According to recent reports, for Meghan, 45, spending the holidays at home also means keeping things simple during a difficult stretch for her family. Her estranged father, Thomas Markle Sr., was arrested in Florida in early November on a federal charge involving child sexual abuse material.

“Everything going on with her dad is still weighing heavily on her,” a source told People. “She wants the holidays to be as quiet and enjoyable as possible for the family.

“Traveling back and forth would be too much for everyone,” the source added.

Since Archie, 7, and Lilibet, 5, returned to school, Meghan and Harry have been making more time for meals out together.

The source told People that one thing the couple appreciate about their new home is the privacy they enjoy nearby.

“They can go out for lunch or dinner, and people give them space,” the insider added.

Recent findings suggest that the children joined their parents for a night out in London on Nov. 18, when Hyde Park’s Winter Wonderland opened for the season. Harry and Archie took a spin on the bumper cars during what People described as the first public sighting of the children since the move.

According to recent reports, christmas in Britain will be a first for both children, even though Archie was born there. He spent his first Christmas in Canada in 2019, and the couple later settled in California, where Lilibet was born in 2021.

Meghan spent Christmas at Sandringham with Harry and the royal family in 2017 and 2018. Neither child has taken part in the gathering, which traditionally includes a Christmas morning church service.

This year, the Sussexes are expected to celebrate at their own home, according to People.

As for what the children are hoping to wake up to on Christmas morning, Harry told "This Morning," “I think they’re looking forward to snow.”.

The news of their holiday looks comes after it was revealed that they reportedly moved into a upcoming Cotswolds home on their friend's estate.

After making the move across the pond in August, the couple was living "in the main house" of their pal's sprawling property.

However, now, their living situation has reportedly changed, with the Daily Mail reporting that they have moved to another property "on the estate.".

According to the outlet, the friend is a wealthy businessman whom Harry befriended through their mutual support for various charities.

Harry and Meghan were rumored to have been house hunting, with several reports noting that the former actress was even looking to replicate the luxury they had in their Montecito, CA, mansion.

The duchess reportedly wants the U.K. residence to boast nine bedrooms—the same number as their California estate—as well as plenty of luxurious amenities.

The news of their move came mere weeks after Harry opened up about their decision to leave California behind and relocate their family to the U.K., revealing that their children's education and his desire to reconnect with his roots played a major role in the decision.

In an interview with GQ that was filmed in September but released only recently, Harry explained that the opportunity to enroll his children in British schools was particularly meaningful to him.

“Opportunities for the family, being able to put the kids in a British school has meant a lot to me. I didn’t know how important it was to me,” he mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that “I always thought it was going to be something that I would try to do or that we would try to do, but now they’ve been in school for two weeks. They’re loving it, and it’s just giving them a whole different experience.”.

Sources indicate that harry emphasized that his decision was not a criticism of the U.S. education system, but rather an opportunity for Archie and Lilibet to experience life in two different countries.

“I’m not criticizing American schools, but I think for kids at 7 and 5 to be able to have that comparison and to have two completely different cultural experiences is so important today,” he explained.

Beyond their education, Harry said returning to Britain has allowed his children to spend more time with relatives and develop closer relationships with family friends.

Sources indicate that another motivation for the move, he explained, was to “be back closer to my family and to be back on U.K. soil for longer than a few days or a week here or there.

“It’s been nice to be close to friends, family, friends and friends and their children as well, to be able to have endless playdates to really, like, help our kids settle in," he said.

Despite the significance of the relocation, Harry admitted that he and Meghan had not necessarily mapped out the move years in advance.

Cigna Group Foundation making $31.5M in grants available to community organizations in 10 states" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

Cigna is making $31.5 million in grant funding available over the next three years to nonprofits in 10 states that are aiming to tackle several key community health priorities.

It has been revealed that the tech giant noted that funds will be made available through its philanthropic arm, the Cigna Group Foundation, with applications open now through Dec. 18. Cigna said in an announcement that it's looking for organizations tackling youth mental health, veteran wellness and the impact of complex health needs on patients and their caregivers.

Cigna remarked the program seeks to deepen the organization's community health strategy to address critical challenges.

The manufacturer first launched a new approach to community health and engagement in 2024, and since then has deployed more than $30 million in funding to 190 nonprofit organizations. Projects backed by these grants have reached at least 321,000 people, Cigna said.

It has been revealed that "Over the past several years, we’ve seen the tangible impact we can make when we invest in strong nonprofit partners and come together to help communities achieve better health and vitality," noted Melissa Skottegaard, board chair of The Cigna Group Foundation, in the announcement. "We’re building on what’s working, bringing together funding, collaboration and the skills of our employee volunteers to address some of the most pressing health challenges facing communities across the street and around the world.".

Cigna will allot $10.5 million to each of the three focus areas under the initiative, per the announcement. Youth mental health, for example, has been a leading topic at the firm for some time, and the company stated it will also continue to build on its partnership with the Boys and Girls Clubs of America in this area.

Recent findings suggest that in that partnership, Cigna has helped build out trauma-informed care services to 90% of clubs, reaching 11,000 employees. The company stated that these efforts have supported 1,600 youths, and that its workforce has contributed more than 2,000 hours to local clubs.

According to recent reports, eligible organizations can apply for two-year, $250,000 grants to support programs in the three categories. The funds will be available to groups in Arizona, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Missouri, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Tennessee and Texas, per the announcement.

Cigna said its foundation will also continue to support community health through its Health Equity Impact Fund.

According to recent reports, "Community organizations can be a powerful source of support for people navigating complex health conditions,” said Matt Perlberg, president of Evernorth Pharmacy & Care Delivery and board member of the Cigna Group Foundation, in the announcement. “By helping patients and caregivers connect with resources and overcome barriers to care, these organizations can provide important support alongside essential medical treatment, helping people navigate their health and care journey.”.

Sources indicate that XRP is having its worst November on record, but one prominent crypto entrepreneur still sees a four-digit price ahead. EasyA co-founder Dom Kwok has reiterated his $1,000 XRP target for 2030, even as the token crashes toward $0.90 and institutional investors pull money from spot exchange-traded funds (ETFs).

Recent findings suggest that XRP has dropped 25% this month, surpassing its previous November record decline in 2019. The token briefly touched $0.862 over the weekend before recovering toward $0.94. It remains below $1, a level XRP has failed to reclaim since November 14.

The timing makes Kwok’s forecast look almost absurd on a chart. Yet the sell-off is now testing a level where historical capitulation, ETF positioning, and XRP’s long-term adoption thesis collide.

In a recent development, the institutional story has taken a serious hit, with spot XRP ETFs recording $30.76 million in November outflows, marking their third consecutive week of withdrawals. Assets across the funds have slipped from around $1.42 billion at October’s end to below $1 billion.

Sources indicate that november has also produced no daily net inflow for XRP ETFs so far. That is a sharp reversal from the buying streak that helped fuel institutional optimism earlier this year. Still, cumulative net inflows remain near $1.78 billion since launch. Investors have pulled money recently, but the institutional trade has not disappeared.

Right now, XRP’s chart is already showing signs of trying to stabilize. The token has bounced from its weekend low around $0.86, with buyers defending the $0.90 area. The daily Relative Strength Index sits near 32, following its recent oversold dip below 30.

That is not a confirmed reversal. But XRP does not need a massive catalyst to produce a sharp bounce after a decline this aggressive.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 18:49 EST / NOVEMBER 23 2026.

Six months after its last funding round, artificial intelligence startup Sierra Technologies Inc. today revealed that it has closed a $1.75 billion late-stage investment.

It has been revealed that greenoaks and Lightspeed led the Series F deal. They were joined by a group of returning backers that included Alphabet Inc.’s GV fund.

It has been revealed that sierra sells a set of cloud services that enables workers to create AI agents without writing code. The centerpiece of the suite is Ghostwriter, which can automatically generate agents based on user-provided prompts and files. A software team, for example, could upload a set of bug reports and request an agent that can automatically group them by problem type.

Ghostwriter checks the dataset that users upload for formatting errors before putting it to use. Once an agent is ready, the tool simulates user conversations to find potential bugs. Ghostwriter places particular emphasis on edge cases, unusual requests that can trip up an agent if they’re not addressed during development.

Sierra also offers a second development tool called Horizon. It can be used to create agents that automate time-consuming tasks. A marketing team could build an agent that monitors user interactions with a product page over several months, finds areas for improvement and automatically makes the necessary optimizations.

Sources indicate that sierra powers customers’ agents using more than a dozen large language models. Simple requests are sent to latency-optimized LLMs, while more complex queries are processed by pricier frontier models. Sierra indicates that it also uses several internally developed algorithms.

Customers can manage their AI projects using a third Sierra product called Agent Studio. According to the company, it includes over 40 connectors that enable agents to retrieve information from external systems. There’s also a tool for building custom connectors.

Agent Studio detects gaps in agents’ knowledge. Furthermore, it can automatically fix some of those gaps. The platform detects when a human support representative answers a customer inquiry that the help desk hasn’t encountered before and turns it into a knowledge base article. From there, agents can use the article to answer similar requests.

The studio also lends itself to certain other tasks. A collaboration feature enables multiple team members to review agent updates before they roll out to production. If a technical concern makes it past the review, developers can use a debugging tool to study what went wrong. The tool displays every single step of the workflow through which an agent processes prompts.

Rounding out Sierra’s product portfolio is an AI assistant called Explorer. It can proactively flag notable business events without a prompt and search through a organization’s internal datasets. In some cases, it also generates business advice.

It has been revealed that sierra’s latest raise, its third in 14 months, comes a few weeks after its annualized revenue topped $400 million. The organization disclosed at the time that it had added nearly half the sum over the preceding quarter. Its customer base now includes half the Fortune 50.

Sierra will reportedly use the latest funding to enhance its product portfolio and hire more salespeople.
